fieldMarks: Slender garter-snake relative, typically about 3 ft (max recorded snout-vent 1250 mm); dark brown or black back with lighter side stripes.
Underside pale, usually light yellow or green; tail about 30% of body length and relatively long muzzle.
Large paired parietal spots; reduced or absent broad brown ventrolateral stripe that the very similar eastern ribbon snake shows.
behavior: Semi-aquatic and fast; dives into water or vanishes into brush or crevices when disturbed; active by day in warm periods.
Forages for frogs by making closed-mouth head thrusts in sets of three to flush them; amphibians make up an estimated 80-92% of the diet, with fish, snails and eggs also taken.
Active March to October in the north; hibernates in rocky outcrops or crevices, sometimes with other snakes and may migrate between winter and summer habitats.
habitat: Brushy habitats near streams, ponds, lakes, sloughs, ditches, swamps and marshes, often in water-edge vegetation; hibernation sites may be upland away from water.
range: Central United States (NatureServe: Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin); Animal Diversity Web adds the range south through Mexico into Central America; not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Eastern ribbon snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Eastern has a broad brown ventrolateral stripe; western has paired large parietal spots, a longer muzzle and longer tail (Animal Diversity Web).
